issues.description: AlterTable contract weakened: replacing outer Delimited with OneOf silently drops support for comma-chained heterogeneous alterations
issues.detail: The previous grammar wrapped the OneOf in Delimited(...), which contractually allowed sequences like 'ALTER TABLE t ADD col_b ... CONSTRAINT ..., DROP COLUMN a, DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS c'. The new grammar removes the outer Delimited and only permits a single top-level action per ALTER TABLE statement (with inner Delimited only inside DROP COLUMN / DROP CONSTRAINT / ADD). The PR also deletes the test fixture that previously exercised the chained form. From the ADT/LSP lens this is a contract narrowing: callers that previously parsed correctly will now fail. T-SQL does accept comma-delimited mixed alterations of this shape, so the supertype contract ('ALTER TABLE accepts a delimited list of actions') has been weakened to a subtype contract ('exactly one top-level action, with delimited lists only inside DROP'). Either restore the outer Delimited or document explicitly that mixed chains are unsupported and justify why the removed fixture was actually invalid.

issues.description: IdentityGrammar accepts ill-formed inputs: SignedSegmentGrammar treated as freestanding optional rather than bound to its literal
issues.detail: The new IdentityGrammar contract is 'IDENTITY ( [sign] number , [sign] number )'. But because each SignedSegmentGrammar is an independent optional Ref rather than fused to its NumericLiteralSegment (e.g. via a Sequence or a SignedNumericLiteral ADT), the grammar does not express the real invariant that the sign belongs to the number. The right abstraction is a SignedNumericLiteral ADT (sign optionally prepended to a numeric literal, treated as a single value) used in both seed and increment positions, mirroring how negative literals are handled elsewhere. As written the abstraction leaks the lexer's two-token representation through the parse tree (sign_indicator + numeric_literal as siblings) rather than presenting a single signed-number value to downstream rules. This will bite any rule that wants to read the seed value.

issues.description: DEFAULT_LANGUAGE now accepts NumericLiteralSegment without justification or test coverage
issues.detail: The CreateLoginStatement _default_language contract was widened to accept NumericLiteralSegment in addition to QuotedLiteralSegment and NakedIdentifierSegment. The PR description mentions only the unquoted identifier case, and the added test fixture exercises only 'DEFAULT_LANGUAGE=us_english'. If the numeric form is a real T-SQL form (LCID), add a fixture; if it isn't, drop it. Contract widenings without tests become permanent drift.

issues.description: DeclareStatement table-body contract: TableIndexSegment added to the OneOf without specifying ordering/multiplicity invariants
issues.detail: TableIndexSegment is appended to the OneOf inside the table-body Delimited. The implicit contract is now 'any interleaving of columns, constraints, computed columns, and indexes, in any order, any count'. T-SQL actually permits indexes inline with columns, but the spec for this module should state the invariant explicitly (in a comment) — at minimum that index entries are siblings of column definitions rather than nested inside them. Without a stated invariant, future contributors will not know whether to add inline-index syntax under ColumnDefinitionSegment or here.

review.summary: From the ADT/contract lens, the most important issue is a silent contract narrowing in AlterTableStatementSegment: removing the outer Delimited around the OneOf changes the supertype's promise from 'a delimited list of alterations' to 'exactly one top-level alteration', and the PR deletes the fixture that exercised the wider form rather than justifying it as invalid. The IdentityGrammar change works for the test case but leaks the lexer's two-token sign representation through the parse tree instead of introducing a proper SignedNumericLiteral ADT; downstream rules will see sign and value as siblings. The CreateLogin widenings are mostly fine but the DEFAULT_LANGUAGE numeric branch is added without test coverage or justification. Overall: the new functionality is welcome, but two of the contracts changed shape in ways that deserve either explicit justification or a tighter abstraction.
